Justin Trudeau on politics, a famous father and the oil sands

Thought this was interesting when I saw it on the other site briefly:

I think this is the most him of any interview I've read to date.

  • people have been wondering for a while if the fall of importance liberalism in western politics to populism is in part because it's been so successful. Civil rights in Canada are just not a battle that need to be fought that hard anymore, so why would we need a standard bearer? Not forgetting the trans community, the shift of liberation from (oppression) to liberation to (pursuit of opportunity) was kind of what I was thinking would happen as well. This is where negative income taxes and working income tax benefits are going to need to play a bigger role in years to come I think, we'll see where he goes with it I guess.

  • his description of the role of the local representative and the importance of actually talking to people jives with why I thought he was so adamant about open nominations. Not because of some high fallutin democratic ideal but because he believes nominees need learn to become the citizens' voice instead of treating them as a lever to power. Lots of conversations.

  • first piece of legislation to fix: C51. Interesting choice...

  • language about Quebec. I think this is consistent with how Quebeckers see ourselves, but it is less consistent with how we see the Liberal party. It's certainly not how the BQ and NDP will frame the LPC's efforts in la belle province. He'll have a lot of work to do to prove this one.

I really liked this interview. I actually contributed to the liberals last year, but their vote on C51 disappointed me so completely, that I'm not sure I can vote for them this cycle.

Justin, please do not give up and keep plugging. If you keep banging this drum, you will get your chance. More Canadians need to believe in you, and we need to see the results of your new inclusiveness. However, i think the NDP are making a very strong case why it should be their turn this cycle.

For the record, I am not a leftwing nut or conservative crackpot. I've voted for all parties at least twice in federal elections over the years.
Parkinsons and depression drugs can alter moral judgment, study shows

Sometimes I really wonder about study design in psych experiments. They seem so odd sometimes. Can you really make big inferences about complex emotions and behaviors by boiling it down to pain and money? I see the basis for the study in the link between people taking the drug an behaviors, but they only gave people a single dose, and a lot of psych drugs have a very different effect as they build up than they do in a single dose. The method just seems odd to me.
